newsitem.title: GREECE: U.S. dollar to rise vs mark ahead of EMU-Chase.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dollar to rise vs mark ahead of EMU-Chase.

text.p: Tighter EU fiscal policy, along with a more accomodative monetary stance and a desire for more competitive mark-block exchange rates all point to a stronger dollar during the transition to EMU, a senior economist at Chase Manhattan Bank in London said.

"Cyclical positions of economies and policy settings suggest that the dollar will rally against the mark-block during the transition to EMU," said Robin Marshall, head of European Economic Research at Chase Manhattan Bank in London.

Speaking at a conference organised by the Hellenic American Chamber of Commerce and the Hellenic Bank Association, Marshall said the combination of stricter fiscal and looser monetary policy in the EU coupled with higher European unemployment also supported a stronger dollar.
Marshall said he saw the dollar rising to around 1.60 marks in twelve months time from levels of around 1.55 currently.
